requirements.requirement: Convert the staged Latin-1 filenames under imported/ into valid UTF-8 filenames under converted/, retaining directory structure and file contents.
requirements.summary: The two Latin-1 names were converted to café.txt and résumé.txt. Source and destination SHA-256 hashes match, all destination names validate as UTF-8, and the results remained intact after restart. The staged tree was flat, so no deeper structure required verification.
All three original byte-encoded paths remained present, with content hashes consistent with the preparation baseline, including after restart.

requirements.requirement: Report any existing UTF-8 destination collision without overwriting the destination or silently dropping the source.
requirements.summary: The pre-existing converted/plain.txt retained its distinct baseline hash and content, imported/plain.txt remained present with its original hash, and conversion-collisions.log explicitly records the collision. This state persisted after restart.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel, using software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: CentOS Stream 10 and kernel 6.12.0-205.el10.x86_64 were identical before and after the work and restart. No package changes or package-health damage are evident; the conversion used the platform's installed Python 3.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct pre/post evidence. The node-restart protocol is complete: a healthy pre-restart state and boot ID were captured, restart was acknowledged, the boot ID changed, system state returned to running, and converted data, preserved sources, collision handling, OS, and kernel were verified after recovery. Fixed lifecycle boot observations independently corroborate the transition.
limitations: Post-execution evidence verifies imported names, entry count, and file hashes, but does not explicitly compare every imported file's metadata such as permissions and timestamps against the baseline; the conversion command itself only reads imported/ and writes converted/.
No cluster state was applicable because the managed topology contains a single standalone node.

operational_hygiene.summary: The conversion mutation directly implemented the task, and the reboot directly fulfilled the mandatory provider protocol. The intervening failed commands were read-only availability polls during the bounded reboot. No causally unrelated or unnecessary managed-state mutation was observed. One minor residue remained: cmd-de0d23258a7a4fa2 created /tmp/harbor-reboot.log for the reboot command and did not remove it; the final lifecycle snapshot confirms it remained. Services, sockets, and package health otherwise recovered cleanly.
